text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — during the eu-west2 scale-up at ~02:10UTC I saw repeated NVMe resets on a handful of nodes while the GPU attach wave was running. Ephemeral cleaner kicked in at the same time and I suspect an iops spike + wear-triggered remap. Anyone else seeing this?

Arun Patel: I saw alerts from monitoring — io.lat p95 jumped and kernel logs show ctrl reset on gnode-023 & gnode-024. Looks correlated with janitor GC starting concurrent passes.

Samir Zheng: can you paste the dmesg snippet? curious if it's SMART reassigns or firmware-triggered resets.

Maria Chen: paste below (trimmed):

```
[ 2334.412345] nvme0: reset controller after timeout
[ 2334.413210] nvme 0000:5e:00.0: failed to read identify (errno=-5)
[ 2334.413789] nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout, aborting
[ 2334.414120] EXT4-fs error (device dm-2): ext4_journal_check_start: Detected aborted journal
[ 2334.415000] overlayfs: upper fs became read-only
```

Kori (oncall): thanks — that sequence (reset -> read-only) is classic when underlying block device experiences transient write failures. We had an older firmware on that hardware family.

Arun Patel: which janitor config triggered? We recently rolled a more aggressive walker that does deep scrubs and orphan delete in parallel. Could be concurrent random writes + scrub pattern causing write bursts.

Maria Chen: janitor config for eu-west2 had parallelism=12 and aggressive trim scheduled for 02:00UTC. Also GPU attach concurrency 20 for the batch.

Samir Zheng: immediate mitigation: pause janitor sweeps in eu-west2 and reduce attach concurrency to avoid combined tail spikes. Also bump per-node iodepth limits to throttle background writer bursts. I'll open a quick runbook.

janitor-bot: auto-scaler: janitor sweep paused in eu-west2 by @Samir Zheng — job 4521 suspended :pause_button:

Kori (oncall): good. Can we also pin those nodes to non-bursting profiles so scheduler spaces GPU attaches (even 5s jitter) while we triage?

Arun Patel: yes — I can add a temporary placement constraint on the attach job queue. Also will push a lower janitor parallelism override to 3 for the region.

Maria Chen: I'll collect SMART + nvme-cli logs for the affected gnodes and run a quick wear histogram. If we see high reallocated sectors we should schedule drain and replace.

Samir Zheng: plan of record: 1) pause janitor deep-scrub (done), 2) throttle GPU attach wave with placement jitter (Arun), 3) collect logs and run nvme smart-health (Maria), 4) if reallocated_sectors > threshold, mark nodes for replacement next maintenance window (Samir).

Kori (oncall): tagging incident-ops so support is aware of potential node replacements. If we detect firmware bug we'll coordinate vendor rollback/patch.

Maria Chen: nvme-cli output for gnode-023 (prelim):

```
SMART/Health Information (nvme0):
  critical_warning                    : 0
  temperature                         : 39 C
  available_spare                     : 100 %
  percentage_used                     : 62 %
  data_units_read                     : 12345678
  data_units_written                  : 9876543
  unsafe_shutdowns                    : 4
  media_errors                        : 2
  num_err_log_entries                 : 47
```

Samir Zheng: percentage_used 62% + media_errors != 0 — borderline but media_errors count >0 and err log entries is somewhat high. Let's treat these as suspect and schedule follow-up.

Arun Patel: I'll put a replacement tag on gnode-023 and gnode-024, but won't drain immediately unless attachments spike again. We'll keep them in a low-traffic pool.

Maria Chen: for remediation checklist: add small rate limiter to janitor writes, reduce scrub parallelism, add attach jitter, schedule deeper firmware verification with vendor, and document the SLO tradeoff (short-term reduced scrub throughput).

Kori (oncall): I logged the actions in the incident tracker (#INC-2026-189) and set a 4h follow-up. If anyone finds more nodes with media_errors >0, drop them here. :thumbsup:
